title: TRACE: Your Diffusion Model is Secretly an Instance Edge Detector
claim: Instance boundaries emerge at a specific diffusion step in self-attention, which can be detected and distilled into an edge decoder.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, attention-map rows over timesteps, green checkmark callouts
description: The figure has two halves. On the left, a red arrow labeled 'Reverse Process, Prompt: Two Cats' runs from a noise image (τ=999) to a clean cat photo (τ=0). Below it are two rows of attention maps at τ=999, 699, 499 and 99. The top row is self-attention and the bottom row is cross-attention. Self-attention at τ=699 has a yellow border and a dashed white box. It shows two cats separated into different colors, with red 'Temporal Difference' arrows beside it. Cross-attention stays semantic, as blobs on the cats' faces. On the right, a green arrow labeled 'Forward Process, Prompt: Null-Text' runs from a dog photo back to noise. Below it are self-attention maps at τ=99, 199, 399 and 799. The map at τ=399 is outlined in green and labeled 'Instance Emergence Point'. Green rounded boxes labeled 'Attention Boundary Divergence' and 'One-step Edge Distillation' lead from that map to edge maps. The edge map with red X marks (noisy) is contrasted with the one with green circles (clean).
caption: Emergence and extraction of instance cues in diffusion attention. (a) In reverse process, cross-attention remains semantic even with the prompt, whereas self-attention at specific steps reveals instance-level structure. (b) TRACE selects the instance-emergent step using a temporal divergence criterion, extracts non-parametric edges from self-attention differences, and refines them via a one-step distillation with the diffusion backbone to refine instance boundaries.
abstract: High-quality instance and panoptic segmentation has traditionally relied on dense instance-level annotations such as masks, boxes, or points, which are costly, inconsistent, and difficult to scale. Unsupervised and weakly-supervised approaches reduce this burden but remain constrained by semantic backbone constraints and human bias, often producing merged or fragmented outputs. We present TRACE (TRAnsforming diffusion Cues to instance Edges), showing that text-to-image diffusion models secretly function as instance edge annotators. TRACE identifies the Instance Emergence Point (IEP) where object boundaries first appear in self-attention maps, extracts boundaries through Attention Boundary Divergence (ABDiv), and distills them into a lightweight one-step edge decoder. This design removes the need for per-image diffusion inversion, achieving 81x faster inference while producing sharper and more connected boundaries. On the COCO benchmark, TRACE improves unsupervised instance segmentation by +5.1 AP, and in tag-supervised panoptic segmentation it outperforms point-supervised baselines by +1.7 PQ without using any instance-level labels. These results reveal that diffusion models encode hidden instance boundary priors, and that decoding these signals offers a practical and scalable alternative to costly manual annotation.
